name: FluxPoint Energy
about: FluxPoint Energy, based in Houston and McLean, Virginia, plans what it expects to be the first new US uranium conversion plant in more than 70 years, in Texas: converting uranium oxide into uranium hexafluoride (UF6), the feedstock that enrichment plants process into reactor fuel. Filed a uranium conversion facility letter of intent with the NRC in April 2026.
expected_reason: Conversion produces the UF6 that enrichers like General Matter buy.

verdict.what_it_builds: A planned uranium conversion plant in Texas that would convert uranium oxide into uranium hexafluoride (UF6), the feedstock that enrichment plants process into reactor fuel. The company filed a uranium conversion facility letter of intent with the NRC in April 2026.
verdict.buyers: Uranium enrichment plants, which take UF6 as feedstock.

overlaps.why: An enrichment operator with a pending NRC license application for its Paducah facility, so it would need UF6 feedstock that FluxPoint would sell. This is a supplier relationship, not head-on, so it is not a portfolio conflict.
Holds an NRC license for its American Centrifuge Plant and has a LEU enrichment master IDIQ, so it would buy UF6 as feedstock.
Holds an NRC license for enrichment and sits on the LEU enrichment master IDIQ, so it is a likely UF6 buyer.

verdict.reasoning: FluxPoint would make UF6, the feedstock enrichment plants buy, so it would sell into the enrichers on the map rather than compete with them. The likely buyers are General Matter (an Anti Fund portfolio company, but a supplier relationship, not a conflict), Centrus, Urenco USA, Orano and Global Laser Enrichment. The lane map does not track conversion producers, so it cannot show whether conversion capacity is already entrenched. The description has no founders, technology or stated technical wedge, so the call is look.
